SELECTED_INDEX: 4
CONFIDENCE: 0.24
EXPLANATION: 1) The presence of weak twin bands at 2719 cm⁻¹ and 2795 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of the Fermi-resonance pair of the aldehydic C–H stretch; only candidates 4, 9 and 10 contain an aldehyde, all others do not.  
2) The C=O stretching band appears at 1727 cm⁻¹ – typical for a non-conjugated aldehyde / saturated ketone; candidate 4 possesses two adjacent carbonyl groups (one aldehyde, one ketone) that would give a single, somewhat broadened Raman band of the right wavenumber and width.  
3) A tert-butyl group gives strong CH₃ symmetric/asymmetric stretches around 2870–2980 cm⁻¹ and intense CH₃ rocking bands near 760–800 cm⁻¹.  The spectrum shows four strong C–H stretches at 2879/2913/2938/2972 cm⁻¹ and two very intense bands at 767 and 800 cm⁻¹, matching the expected t-Bu signatures; only candidate 4 (CC(C)(C)CC(=O)C=O) contains a tert-butyl moiety together with an aldehyde.  
4) Remaining medium bands at 598, 885 and 931 cm⁻¹ can be assigned to C–C–C skeletal bends and CH₃ deformations typical of branched alkanes; no additional hetero-atom stretches (e.g. C–O, N–H, C=N) are required, favouring a simple oxygenated hydrocarbon such as candidate 4 over others with ether or imine/amide groups.  

Taken together, the aldehyde Fermi doublet, a single ~1727 cm⁻¹ carbonyl, and prominent tert-butyl CH₃ features all point to candidate 4 as the best match.
